moat_against: Low switching costs — no lock-in or network effects in peripherals
Platform owners (Apple, Microsoft) and PC OEMs (HP, Dell) compete adjacently, plus Razer/Corsair and low-cost rivals
Tariff exposure on China-made hardware — policy swings hit results both ways (Q1 FY27 $61M refund)
Cyclical demand: OE/share fell from $7.55 (FY21) to $0.68 (FY22); supplier incident pressures Q2/Q3 FY27 revenue
moat_for: #1 global share in most core categories, with share gains again in Q4 FY26
Brand, industrial design and 100+ country retail/enterprise distribution
Gross margin recovered 37.88% (FY23) to 43.20% (FY26) — some pricing power
Debt-free asset-light model: capex ~$62M on $4.84B revenue, $1.74B cash
moat_justification: Durable #1 share in mice/keyboards/gaming/video collaboration and high measured ROIC through the cycle (roic_proxy 0.33 trough FY23 to 1.42 FY26), but the capital base is tiny by construction so ROIC overstates the franchise; gross margin is hardware-like (37.9%-43.2%), switching costs are low, there are no network effects, and leadership must be re-won every product cycle.
name: Logitech International S.A.
one_liner: High-quality debt-free peripherals leader, moat 5/10 — but at $104.41 it prices in the bull case: weighted IRR 8.6%, IV@15% $50.50; it only clears 15% at/below ~$50.
